coreClasses.qualification: Pre-existing independently compiled corrected M3 candidate classes; current owner template compiled beside probe. This is isolated diagnostic materialization, not the final named recipe application.

preliminaryWarmupSensitivity.initialPlan: Warm six rounds and measure eight rounds at 4096, then repeat at 65536.
preliminaryWarmupSensitivity.observedReasonForRevision: At 4096, the Eclipse update had a median 524288 allocated bytes; at 65536 it had zero. The final plan warms the entire size corpus first. Both raw runs are retained; no rounds were excluded within either run.
preliminaryWarmupSensitivity.interpretation: The difference is consistent with warmup/JIT escape-analysis sensitivity; no compiler trace was captured to identify the exact optimization.

structuralSourceEvidence.observation: Parallel primitive int count/flag columns at existing M3 key-only stable slots; no per-key count wrapper is stored.
Key-only Table uses reference and primitive arrays, with values array left empty; geometric array growth is included in admission allocation.
Default linked multiset constructs a LinkedHashMap<E, Count> backing map.
Admission creates Count(occurrences) for a newly distinct key.
Stores Map<E, MutableInteger> and admits one MutableInteger per distinct key.
Uses the donor primitive ObjectIntMaps mutable owner, not a boxed count map.
Count operations delegate to MutableObjectIntMap; this donor already has primitive counters.

limitations: Single shared-container JVM execution, not JMH, not a replicated statistical performance result.
All headline numbers are observed samples; they do not establish a universal speed, heap-size or scaling claim.
Default-capacity growth makes construction allocation include discarded intermediate arrays and tables.
M3 includes stable insertion order and flag columns; Apache HashMultiSet and Eclipse HashBag do not offer that feature combination.
Allocation meters exclude work on GC/JIT threads and do not measure retained graph size.
Current-thread CPU excludes CPU of other threads; wall time can include pauses and scheduling delays.
No JNI kernel, native memory, concurrency, null keys, full removals, provider views, bulk operations, presizing or large-count overflow measured.
Count samples use bounded positive counts for common semantics; existing separate differential tests own edge contracts.
Warmup is finite and does not prove every hot method has reached its final compilation tier.
